# SupportForge Gotchas

> Known SupportForge (remote endpoint agent) patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [&quot;Online&quot; agent at near-full disk is a heartbeat, not a working executor](online-flag-vs-hung-executor.md): a SupportForge agent at sub-1% free disk reports online but its executor is hung — one command completes per session, then "Session not found or has ended"; relieve disk out-of-band before remediating. HIGH.
- [execute_command can return another session's output when multiple agent connections are open](execute-command-cross-session-output.md): with 2+ concurrent agent connections, a correctly-targeted execute_command can silently return a different session's output; prefix every remote command with a hostname echo and verify it before trusting or acting on the result. HIGH.
- [Portal backend outpaces its UI — audit route payloads before scoping "missing" reports as backend work](portal-backend-outpaces-ui.md): the customer portal's endpoints often already return the data a "missing" report needs (fields, filters, pagination) — read the route/service payload before planning new endpoints, syncs, or migrations. MEDIUM.
- [get_ticket(N) resolves the internal id before the MSP number and can return a different client's ticket](get-ticket-id-vs-msp-number-collision.md): The URL number is an msp_ticket_number, but get_ticket resolves the internal id first; legacy Zendesk-imported rows have small ids in the same range, so get_ticket(195) silently returns another client's closed 2025 ticket. Resolve via list_tickets(search:"#N") then fetch by internal id, and assert organization_name matches before acting on an endpoint. HIGH.
- [list_tickets excludes closed but still returns solved, padding any open-work view](list-tickets-includes-solved.md): "closed are excluded" does not mean finished work is filtered out — solved is a separate terminal status that comes back by default, so an unfiltered queue silently mixes completed tickets into open work (45 rows vs 4 on the same query). Always pass an explicit status list. HIGH.
- [get_ticket_messages limit truncates from the oldest end, hiding the newest replies](get-ticket-messages-limit-truncates-oldest.md): messages are oldest-first and limit is a head cut, so lowering limit to dodge the oversized-payload error silently drops the most recent messages and inverts who-is-waiting-on-whom; keep the limit high and grep the saved payload for direction/stripped_text instead. HIGH.
- [Landing a local file on an endpoint via write_file: chunk it and verify](write-file-chunk-verify-transfer.md): write_file is the only inbound primitive and a single large base64 blob gets a char dropped/duplicated in reproduction (mod-4 failure, silent 0-byte file); split into ~2KB chunks with per-chunk SHA256 and a final md5 == source check. MEDIUM.
- [Ticket aggregates scoped by a single key (client_id or organization_id) silently undercount](single-key-ticket-aggregates-undercount.md): tickets are dual-keyed — native rows carry client_id ("org_..."), PSA-imported rows carry organization_id (prefix stripped) — so any report scoped by one key returns plausible-but-wrong counts (Reports said 1 created, Tickets said 12, same org/window); scope every aggregate with (client_id = $1 OR organization_id = $2) AND deleted_at IS NULL. HIGH.
- ["Launch was never delivered" is a stale command socket, not an offline machine](agent-stale-command-socket.md): connect_agent's two failure texts mean opposite things — "is offline" = unreachable, "launch was never delivered / no API instance holds this agent's command socket" = the machine is UP and only the socket is stale (commonly after an agent self-update). Restart the SupportForgeAgent service out-of-band via the RMM service-control endpoint; cross-check against a second agent to tell a slept machine from a stale socket. HIGH.
- [An organization's "users" count means recent requesters, not members](org-user-counts-are-recent-requesters.md): total_users on the organizations list and GET /organizations/:id/users both fold a one-year ticket EXISTS into what they call "users", so a 40-contact client reads as 12 — and the browse list applies the same default, so the count and the list agree with each other while both disagree with reality; return member_count and active_requester_count separately and carry `all=1` on any link to the users list. HIGH.
